surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between TMA and surface hydroxyl groups followed by water pulse to regenerate OH sites.
evidence: Due to low surface migration of Al atoms and gas parasitic reaction between trimethyl aluminum (TMA) and NH3, it is very difficult to grow high-quality AlN layer on sapphire, the current main substrate for III-nitride devices. An effective method is to use a pulsed atomic layer epitaxy (PALE) method in the growth of AlN or high Al content AlGaN, which was proposed and realized by Khan et al. This method is via a separate supply of group III and group V sources to enhance the Al atom migration and suppress the gas phase reactions.
